lead: inemaccbot is a Telegram gateway with a durable queue: you send the request from your phone and your computer (or a VPS) runs it as an agent. In this lesson you install it, pair the bot with your chat, and leave it running as a service.
objetivo: install inemaccbot, pair it with your chat, and see /ping respond in Telegram.
hero_alt: Small computer turned on with discreet LEDs and a phone showing a conversation.

aprende.t: The pieces: Telegram, queue, worker, agent
The prerequisites and what breaks without each one
Start it by hand, then as a service

secoes.sub: From your phone to the result.

nos.detalhe: You write to your bot on Telegram, from wherever you are. Only chats on the allowlist get a response; any other chat is silently rejected.
It receives the message, checks the allowlist, understands the command, and turns the request into a task. It's also the one that tells you in the chat when the task finishes.
Five queues, each with its own limit of tasks at the same time. The database saves the request before it runs and recovers whatever was in flight after a crash.
The worker hands the task to the command-line agent, through your subscription. claude is the default; codex is switched on per task with | motor=codex.
When the task finishes, the result comes back to the chat: text directly, a small file as an attachment, and a large video as a link.

secoes.legenda: Click each block. To install and use it, you don't need to touch the code: only the .env and Telegram.

secoes.sub: Tested on Ubuntu with Node 24. The shortcut ./scripts/instalar.sh does the mechanical part and stops at what needs you.

texto: Node 22 or newer (node -v; Ubuntu 24.04 ships 18). claude installed and logged in: check with claude auth status; installed is not the same as authenticated. ffmpeg and python3 for the audio and video tasks.
Without claude logged in, the bot starts and accepts commands, but every agent job fails. It's the most confusing failure, because everything looks right.
Clone the repository and run npm ci (not npm install: ci follows the lockfile, so the install is the same on every machine).
Also clone the domain repos promoavatar and promoavatar3 as sibling folders. Without them the bot starts, but the flows break in the first phase and dozens of tests fail.
Talk to @BotFather, send /newbot, and save the token it gives back. That value is the BOT_TOKEN.
The token is a secret: it never goes into Git, a screenshot, or a message.
Copy the .env.example, protect it with chmod 600, and fill in BOT_TOKEN, QUEUE_DB, STATE_DIR, and LOG_FILE.
In ALLOWED_CHAT_IDS, leave 0. That's pairing mode: the first /ping registers your chat as the owner and closes the door. Empty is not pairing: it's an error on purpose, and the bot won't start.

exemplo.texto: While the allowlist is 0, whoever sends /ping first takes the bot. Pair before you leave it running.

texto: Run npm test and npm run build, then start it by hand with ./start.sh to see any errors on screen.
Send /ping to your bot. It replies with the chat id and saves that id in the .env. From then on, only you are served.
For the bot to survive logout and start by itself at boot, install the user service and turn on linger. On a VPS, use the system service (deploy/inemaccbot-sistema.service).
Never run ./start.sh and the service at the same time with the same token: the two fight over the messages and each one loses half. start.sh already refuses to start when the service is active.

secoes.sub: In order. Change only what is indicated.

blocos.conteudo:
cd ~/projetos
git clone https://github.com/inematds/inemaccbot.git
git clone https://github.com/inematds/promoavatar.git
git clone https://github.com/inematds/promoavatar3.git
cd inemaccbot
./scripts/instalar.sh --checar   # only tells you what is missing, changes nothing
npm ci
npm test
npm run build

cp .env.example .env
chmod 600 .env
# edit the .env: BOT_TOKEN=<from BotFather>  ALLOWED_CHAT_IDS=0
./start.sh       # log on screen; Ctrl+C stops it, draining whatever is running
# in Telegram: /ping  →  the bot replies and saves your chat id

mkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user
cp deploy/inemaccbot.service ~/.config/systemd/user/
systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user enable --now inemaccbot
loginctl enable-linger "$USER"
systemctl --user status inemaccbot   # expect: active (running)

abas.html:
The recovery line shows up in the log, even on an empty queue:

boot: recuperação de leases — requeued=0 failed=0

A configuration error takes the process down at this point, on purpose. Read the message before touching anything else.

• config: falta BOT_TOKEN: the .env has no token.
  • Service active but /ping gets no reply: the allowlist has the wrong id (the log shows rejeitada — fora da allowlist).
  • Bot replies, but every job fails: claude is not logged in.
  • tsc: not found during the build: redo it with NODE_ENV=development npm ci --include=dev.

The bot's .env holds configuration: token, allowlist, paths. Keys for other services live in a separate vault, one file per machine with chmod 600, never versioned. Project rule: the .env holds the path and the id; a third party's secret lives in its owner's file.

exercicios.texto: Follow the steps until the bot replies on Telegram. Pair with ALLOWED_CHAT_IDS=0 and check that the .env has chmod 600. Then test /ajuda and /fila.
exercicios.pronto: /ping replies in your Telegram and /fila shows the queues empty.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: The service is active (running), but the bot does not reply to your /ping. What is the most likely cause?
opcoes: The allowlist has an id that is not your chat's.
perguntas.explica: Outside the allowlist, the message is rejected silently and only shows up in the log. Go back to ALLOWED_CHAT_IDS=0, restart and pair again.

perguntas.p: What is the point of leaving ALLOWED_CHAT_IDS=0 on the first start?
opcoes: To open the bot to anyone forever.
So the first /ping registers your chat as the owner and closes the door.
perguntas.explica: It is pairing mode. That is why you need to pair right away: while it is 0, whoever sends /ping first becomes the owner.

perguntas.p: Where should the key for a third-party service that a task uses be kept?
opcoes: In the text of the request sent through Telegram.
In a separate vault, with chmod 600, outside Git.
In the README, so nobody forgets.
perguntas.explica: A secret never goes in versioned text or in a message. The bot's .env holds configuration; a third party's secret lives in the vault.
